questions.question: What is the name of the layer of the Earth's atmosphere where weather phenomena occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Troposphere** is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere and is the region where we live. It contains approximately **75% to 80%** of the total mass of the atmosphere.

• Almost all **weather phenomena**, including cloud formation, rain, snow, and storms, occur in this layer because it contains nearly all of the atmosphere's **water vapor** and **aerosols**.

• In the troposphere, the temperature generally **decreases with altitude** at a rate known as the environmental lapse rate.

• The **Stratosphere** is the layer above the troposphere; it contains the **Ozone Layer** and is relatively stable, which is why commercial jet aircraft often fly in its lower parts to avoid weather disturbances.

• The **Mesosphere** is the third layer where temperatures drop to their lowest in the atmosphere and where most **meteors** burn up upon entry.

• The **Thermosphere** is a high-altitude layer where temperatures increase significantly with height and contains the **Ionosphere**, which is crucial for **radio communication**.

**Additional Information__**

• The boundary that separates the troposphere from the stratosphere is called the **Tropopause**.

• The height of the troposphere varies with latitude; it is thickest at the **Equator** (about 18 km) and thinnest at the **Poles** (about 8 km) due to the differences in solar heating and centrifugal force.

• The **Exosphere** is the outermost layer of the Earth's atmosphere, extending into space, where the air is extremely thin.

• The atmosphere is composed mainly of **Nitrogen** (78%) and **Oxygen** (21%), with trace amounts of other gases like Argon and Carbon Dioxide.
</ul

questions.question: What is the main objective of the 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme launched in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wetland ecosystem protection**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Amrit Dharohar** scheme was officially announced by the Union Finance Minister during the **Union Budget 2023-24**.

• The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the **conservation** and **optimal use of wetlands**, specifically focusing on the **75 Ramsar sites** identified in India at the time of its launch.

• It aims to enhance **biodiversity**, **carbon stock**, and **ecotourism** opportunities while supporting the livelihoods of local communities residing near these wetlands.

• The scheme is set to be implemented over a period of **three years** to ensure the sustainable development of these vital ecosystems.

• While **River conservation** (e.g., Namami Gange), **Wildlife protection** (e.g., Project Tiger), and **Air pollution control** (e.g., NCAP) are important environmental goals, they are managed under different specific government initiatives.

**Additional Information__**

• **Wetlands** are often referred to as the **'kidneys of the landscape'** because of their critical role in water filtration, flood control, and nutrient cycling.

• The **Ramsar Convention** is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, signed in **1971** in **Ramsar, Iran**.

• India has significantly increased its number of **Ramsar sites** in recent years, reaching a total of **85 sites** as of 2024, the highest in South Asia.

• The **Amrit Dharohar** scheme works in synergy with other environmental programs like **MISHTI** (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes), which focuses on mangrove plantation along the coastline.

• The scheme aligns with the **Mission LiFE** (Lifestyle for Environment) movement launched by the Prime Minister to encourage sustainable living.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **correct** about the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)?

options.text: It aims to eliminate tuberculosis in India by the year 2030
The NTEP reported fewer TB cases in 2024 than in 2023 due to reduced screening.
India has developed its first state-wise TB burden estimation model under NTEP.
It focuses solely on vaccination to prevent TB in newborns

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India has developed its first state-wise TB burden estimation model under NTEP.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• India has become the first country in the world to develop a **mathematical model** to estimate the **Tuberculosis (TB) burden** at the state level, allowing for more granular and localized data collection.

• The **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)** aims to eliminate TB in India by the year **2025**, which is five years ahead of the global **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)** target of 2030. Therefore, the statement regarding the 2030 target for India is incorrect.

• The program does not focus solely on vaccination; it is a multi-pronged strategy that includes **early diagnosis**, **prompt treatment** using **DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course)**, and social support systems.

• TB notification rates have generally shown an **upward trend** in recent years due to intensified case-finding and the mandatory notification policy, making the claim of reduced screening in 2024 incorrect.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP)** was renamed the **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)** in 2020 to reflect the government's commitment to eliminating the disease.

• **Nikshay Portal** is the web-based surveillance system used by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to monitor TB patients and their treatment progress across the country.

• The **Nikshay Poshan Yojana** provides a monthly financial incentive of **500 rupees** to TB patients for nutritional support throughout their treatment duration.

• The **Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** was launched to encourage community support for TB patients, where individuals or organizations (known as **Ni-kshay Mitras**) can adopt patients to provide diagnostic, nutritional, or vocational support.

• **World TB Day** is observed annually on **March 24** to raise public awareness about the devastating health, social, and economic consequences of tuberculosis.
</ul

This means that while the general public may not be immediately affected, people with **lung disease**, **asthma**, **children**, and **older adults** are at a greater risk from exposure to ozone or particle pollution. ***Hence, the statement that values above 100 indicate unhealthy air for sensitive groups is correct.***

• An **AQI** value of **25** is well within the **Good** category, indicating very clean air. ***Hence, the option 25 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• In **India**, the **National Air Quality Index (NAQI)** was launched by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** on **17 September 2014**. It was developed as part of the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a **One Color-One Number-One Description** for the common man to judge air quality.

• The **Indian AQI** system categorizes air quality into **six levels**: **Good (0-50)**, **Satisfactory (51-100)**, **Moderately Polluted (101-200)**, **Poor (201-300)**, **Very Poor (301-400)**, and **Severe (401-500)**.

• **Sensitive groups** include individuals with pre-existing **respiratory conditions** like **COPD** or **bronchitis**, **cardiovascular diseases**, **pregnant women**, and **infants** whose lungs are still developing.

questions.question: Which two tectonic plates are responsible for the formation of the Himalayas due to their collision?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian & Eurasian**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Himalayas** were formed due to the **collision** between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**. This is a classic example of a **continent-continent convergent boundary**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Indian & Eurasian.***

• The **Indian Plate** was originally part of the ancient supercontinent **Gondwanaland**. About **200 million years** ago, it broke off and began moving **northward** toward the much larger **Eurasian Plate**.

• Before the collision, a vast sea called the **Tethys Sea** existed between the two plates. As the **Indian Plate** moved north, the sediments at the bottom of the **Tethys Sea** were compressed and uplifted to form the **Himalayan mountain range**.

• The **Indian & African** plates do not collide to form mountains; their interaction is primarily in the **Indian Ocean** along the **Central Indian Ridge**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Eurasian & Australian** plates meet in the **Southeast Asian** region, contributing to the formation of the **Indonesian archipelago** rather than the **Himalayas**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• The **Pacific & Eurasian** plates interact along the **western Pacific**, forming **island arcs** and **oceanic trenches** like the **Japan Trench** through **subduction**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Himalayas** are classified as **Young Fold Mountains** because they were formed relatively recently in the **Earth's** geological history, approximately **40 to 50 million years** ago.

• The mountain range stretches over **2,400 kilometers** and passes through five countries: **India**, **Pakistan**, **China (Tibet)**, **Nepal**, and **Bhutan**.

• The **Himalayas** contain the world's highest peaks, including **Mount Everest**, which stands at **8,848.86 meters** above sea level.

• The **Tibetan Plateau** was also uplifted during this collision and is often referred to as the **'Roof of the World'** due to its high average elevation of over **4,500 meters**.

• The **Indian Plate** continues to move **northward** at a rate of about **5 centimeters per year**, causing the **Himalayas** to rise by approximately **5 to 10 millimeters** annually and making the region seismically active.

**Important Points__**

• **Plate Tectonics Theory:** This scientific theory describes the large-scale motion of seven large plates and several smaller plates of the **Earth's lithosphere**. It was developed in the **1960s** based on the earlier concept of **Continental Drift** proposed by **Alfred Wegener** in **1912**.

• **Types of Boundaries:** There are three main types of tectonic boundaries: **Convergent** (plates collide), **Divergent** (plates move apart), and **Transform** (plates slide past each other). The **Himalayas** are the result of a **Convergent Boundary**.

• **Impact on Climate:** The **Himalayan** range acts as a massive **climatic barrier**, preventing cold **Siberian** winds from entering the **Indian subcontinent** and forcing the **Monsoon** winds to shed their moisture over **India**.

• **River Systems:** Major perennial rivers like the **Indus**, **Ganges**, and **Brahmaputra** originate from the **Himalayan glaciers**, providing water to millions of people in **South Asia**.

questions.question: Which act introduced separate electorates for Hindus and Muslims in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Morley-Minto Reforms 1909**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Morley-Minto Reforms**, officially known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**, introduced the system of **separate electorates** for **Muslims** in **British India**. This meant that **Muslim** representatives were to be elected exclusively by **Muslim voters**.

• The act was named after **Lord Morley**, the then **Secretary of State for India**, and **Lord Minto**, the then **Viceroy of India**. Due to the introduction of this communal representation, **Lord Minto** is often referred to as the **'Father of Communal Electorate'**.

• The **Indian Councils Act 1892** is incorrect because it primarily focused on increasing the number of members in the **Legislative Councils** and introduced a limited and indirect use of **elections**, but it did not establish **separate electorates** based on religion.

• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919** (or the **Government of India Act 1919**) is incorrect as the starting point because it **extended** the principle of **separate electorates** to other communities like **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians**, and **Europeans**, rather than introducing it.

• The **Government of India Act 1935** is incorrect because it was a much later piece of legislation that introduced **Provincial Autonomy** and further extended **separate electorates** to **depressed classes (scheduled castes)**, **women**, and **labor**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Simla Deputation (1906)**: A group of **Muslim** leaders led by the **Aga Khan** met **Lord Minto** in **October 1906** to demand **separate electorates** and **proportional representation** for **Muslims**, which heavily influenced the **1909 reforms**.

• **Expansion of Councils**: The **1909 Act** significantly increased the size of the **Legislative Councils**. The number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from **16 to 60**.

• **Indian Participation**: For the first time, the act provided for the association of **Indians** with the **Executive Councils** of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**. **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** became the first **Indian** to join the **Viceroy’s Executive Council** as a **Law Member**.

• **Powers of Legislators**: The act empowered members of the **Legislative Councils** to ask **supplementary questions** and move **resolutions** on the **budget**, although they were not allowed to vote on the budget as a whole.

**Important Points__**

• The **1919 Act** introduced **Dyarchy** in the provinces, which divided provincial subjects into two parts: **'Transferred'** and **'Reserved'**. This was a major step toward **responsible government** in **India**.

• The **1935 Act** proposed the establishment of an **All-India Federation** consisting of **Provinces** and **Princely States**. It also abolished **Dyarchy** in the provinces and introduced **Provincial Autonomy**.

• The **Indian Councils Act 1892** allowed the councils to discuss the **annual financial statement** (budget) and address questions to the **Executive**, which was a significant advancement over the **1861 Act**.

• The introduction of **separate electorates** in **1909** is widely viewed by historians as a part of the British **'Divide and Rule'** policy, which eventually contributed to the **partition of India** in **1947**.

questions.question: Which act made the 'Governor-General of Bengal' as the 'Governor-General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1833**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Charter Act of 1833**, also known as the **Saint Helena Act 1833**, was a significant constitutional instrument that centralized the administration of **British India**.

• This act redesignated the **Governor-General of Bengal** as the **Governor-General of India**, vesting in him all **civil and military powers**. This was a major step toward the unification of the country under a single authority.

• **Lord William Bentinck** became the **first Governor-General of India** under the provisions of this act.

• The act deprived the **Governor of Bombay** and the **Governor of Madras** of their **legislative powers**, making the Governor-General of India the sole legislative authority for the entire British territory in India.

• It ended the activities of the **East India Company** as a **commercial body**, transforming it into a purely **administrative body**. The company’s territories in India were now held by it in trust for **His Majesty**, his heirs, and successors.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Charter Act of 1813**: This act renewed the **East India Company** charter for another **20 years**. It ended the company’s **trade monopoly** in India, except for trade in **tea** and trade with **China**. It also allotted **one lakh rupees** annually for the promotion of **education** in India and allowed **Christian missionaries** to enter the country.

• **Charter Act of 1853**: This was the last of the series of **Charter Acts** passed by the **British Parliament** between **1793** and **1853**. It separated the **legislative** and **executive functions** of the Governor-General’s council for the first time and introduced an **open competition system** for the selection and recruitment of **civil servants**.

• **Indian Council Act of 1861**: This act is an important landmark in the constitutional history of India as it initiated the process of **decentralization**. It restored the **legislative powers** to the **Bombay** and **Madras** Presidencies. It also introduced the **Portfolio system**, which was pioneered by **Lord Canning** in **1859**.

• **Regulating Act of 1773**: This was the first step taken by the **British Government** to control and regulate the affairs of the **East India Company** in India. It designated the **Governor of Bengal** as the **Governor-General of Bengal** and **Lord Warren Hastings** was the first person to hold this designation.

**Important Points__**

• The **Charter Act of 1833** introduced a **fourth member** to the Governor-General’s Council, known as the **Law Member**. **Lord Macaulay** was appointed as the first Law Member to assist in the codification of laws.

• The act mandated the establishment of the **First Law Commission** in **1834** under the chairmanship of **Lord Macaulay** to codify **Indian laws**, which eventually led to the creation of the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**.

• An attempt was made by the **1833 Act** to introduce a system of **open competition** for the selection of **civil servants**, stating that Indians should not be debarred from holding any place, office, or employment under the Company. However, this provision was negated after opposition from the **Court of Directors**.

• The act also directed the **Governor-General-in-Council** to take steps for the **abolition of slavery** in India, which was eventually abolished in **1843**.

questions.question: Which ruler greatly supported Gandhara art?
questions.solution:

__

• **Kanishka**, the most powerful ruler of the **Kushan Dynasty**, was the greatest patron of **Gandhara Art**. Under his reign in the **1st and 2nd centuries CE**, this school of art reached its zenith. ***Hence, the statement regarding Kanishka is correct.***

• **Gandhara Art** is a unique style of **Buddhist visual art** that developed in the **North-Western** part of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in regions like **Peshawar** and **Taxila** (modern-day **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan**).

• It is famously known as **Greco-Buddhist Art** because it combined **Hellenistic (Greek)** and **Roman** artistic techniques with **Indian Buddhist** themes. The **Buddha** was often depicted with features resembling the Greek god **Apollo**, including wavy hair and muscular anatomy.

• The emergence of **Mahayana Buddhism** during **Kanishka’s** time encouraged the creation of **Buddha** images in human form, replacing the earlier symbolic representations like the **Wheel** or **Footprints**.

• While **Ashoka** was a great promoter of **Buddhism** in the **3rd century BCE**, his artistic contributions were mainly **Stupas** and **Pillars** (Mauryan Art) rather than the specific **Gandhara** style. ***Hence, the option involving Ashoka is incorrect.***

• **Samudragupta** belonged to the **Gupta Dynasty** (the **Golden Age** of India), which patronized the **Mathura** and **Sarnath** schools of art, focusing on indigenous styles rather than the **Gandhara** style. ***Hence, the option involving Samudragupta is incorrect.***

• **Harsha** (Harshavardhana) ruled in the **7th century CE** and was a patron of **Buddhism** and **Nalanda University**, but by his time, the **Gandhara** school had already declined following the **Huna** invasions. ***Hence, the option involving Harsha is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Features of Gandhara Art:** The primary material used in the early phase was **Blue-grey Schist stone**, which was later replaced by **Stucco** (lime plaster). The sculptures are characterized by **realistic anatomy**, **wavy hair**, **large foreheads**, and **heavy drapery** resembling a Roman **Toga**.

• **Kanishka I:** He ascended the throne in approximately **78 CE**, a date that marks the beginning of the **Saka Era**, which is still used by the **Government of India**. He organized the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in **Kundalvana, Kashmir**, where **Buddhism** was formally split into **Hinayana** and **Mahayana** sects.

• **Comparison with Mathura School:** Unlike the **Gandhara School**, which was foreign-influenced, the **Mathura School of Art** was entirely **indigenous**. It used **Spotted Red Sandstone** and produced images of **Buddha**, **Jain Tirthankaras**, and **Hindu Deities**.

• **Geographical Spread:** The **Gandhara** style spread along the **Silk Road** into **Central Asia** and **China**, significantly influencing the **Buddhist art** of those regions. Major archaeological sites include **Bamiyan**, **Hadda**, and **Begram**.

• **Decline:** The school began to decline after the **3rd century CE** and was severely damaged during the **5th century CE** by the invasion of the **White Hunas** (Hephthalites), who destroyed many monasteries and workshops in the **Gandhara** region.

**Important Points__**

• **Kushan Empire:** At its peak under **Kanishka**, the empire extended from **Central Asia** to the **Gangetic Plain**, with capitals at **Purushapura** (Peshawar) and **Mathura**. This vast territory facilitated the exchange of ideas between the **East** and the **West**.

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution provides for the State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Article 168**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 168** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the **constitution of Legislatures in States**. It mandates that for every state, there shall be a legislature consisting of the **Governor** and one or two houses. ***Hence, Article 168 is the correct answer.***
 
• It clarifies that in states where there are two houses, they are known as the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)** and the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)**. In states with only one house, it is the **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Article 170** specifically details the **composition of the Legislative Assemblies**. It stipulates that the Assembly should consist of members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies, with a maximum limit of **500** members and a minimum of **60** members. ***Hence, Article 170 is incorrect as it deals with composition rather than the provision for the house.***
 
• **Article 172** provides for the **duration of State Legislatures**. It states that every Legislative Assembly, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for **five years** from the date appointed for its first meeting. ***Hence, Article 172 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 174** deals with the **sessions of the State Legislature**, including **prorogation** and **dissolution**. It grants the **Governor** the power to summon the House and dissolve the Legislative Assembly. ***Hence, Article 174 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the State Legislature**: 
 
 
• The State Legislature is governed by **Part VI** of the Constitution, spanning from **Article 168 to 212**.
 
• Most Indian states have a **unicameral** system, meaning they only have a **Legislative Assembly**. 
 
• A **bicameral** system exists in only a few states where both a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Legislative Council** are present to ensure broader representation.
 
 
 
• **Membership Qualifications (Article 173)**:
 
 
• To be a member of the **Legislative Assembly**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and at least **25 years** of age.
 
• For the **Legislative Council**, the minimum age requirement is **30 years**.
 
 
 
• **The Legislative Council (Article 169)**:
 
 
• **Article 169** gives **Parliament** the power to **create or abolish** a Legislative Council in a state if the Legislative Assembly of that state passes a resolution by a **special majority**.
 
• Currently, only **six states** have a bicameral legislature: **Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Election**: Members of the **Legislative Assembly (MLAs)** are **directly elected** by the people on the basis of **adult suffrage**. In contrast, members of the **Legislative Council (MLCs)** are **indirectly elected** through a complex process involving local bodies, graduates, teachers, and nomination by the **Governor**.
 
• **Special Provisions for Small States**: While **Article 170** sets a minimum of **60** members for an Assembly, exceptions have been made for smaller states like **Sikkim (32)**, **Goa (40)**, and **Mizoram (40)** through various constitutional amendments to ensure administrative feasibility.
 
• **Officer of the House**: The **Legislative Assembly** is presided over by a **Speaker** and a **Deputy Speaker**, who are elected by the members of the Assembly from among themselves.
 
• **Role of the Governor**: The **Governor** is an integral part of the State Legislature (under **Article 168**) even though he is not a member of either House. No bill can become law without the **Governor's assent**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The Real number system (R) is the universal set containing all Rational (Q) and Irrational (I) numbers.

Hierarchy: Real → Rational → Integers → Whole → Natural.

Since Rational numbers are a subset of Real numbers (Q ⊂ R), every rational number is real.

Integers and whole numbers are rational, not irrational, making other options false.

**∴ The correct answer is All rational numbers are real.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Rational numbers (Q), Irrational numbers (I), and Real numbers (R).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34d98e22305478af6eeec8aa48c06e04d2c4bf25b10523c16c056de246f0e3ee.png] 

⇒ Real numbers (R) = Rational (Q) ∪ Irrational (I).

⇒ This implies Q ⊂ R and I ⊂ R.

⇒ Integers (Z) ⊂ Q (e.g., 5 = 5/1), so integers are rational.

⇒ Whole numbers (W) ⊂ Q (e.g., 0 = 0/1), so whole numbers are rational.

⇒ Therefore, the statement 'All rational numbers are real' is the only true statement.

**∴ The correct answer is All rational numbers are real.**

**__Additional Information__**

Rational Numbers

Numbers that can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Their decimal expansion is either terminating or repeating.

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that cannot be expressed as simple fractions. Their decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-repeating (e.g., √3, π).

Real Numbers

The set of all numbers that can be represented on a number line, including both rational and irrational values.

Integers and Whole Numbers

Whole numbers (0, 1, 2...) and Integers (...−1, 0, 1...) are all rational because they can be written with a denominator of 1.</p

questions.question: The relationship between integers and whole numbers can be expressed as:

options.text: Whole numbers and integers are the same sets
Whole numbers and integers have no elements in common

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Subset Hierarchy**: **Natural Numbers** → **Whole Numbers** → **Integers**.

**Whole Numbers** (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

**Integers** (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

Since every element of **W** is present in **Z**, **W** is a subset of **Z**.

Thus, all whole numbers are integers.

**∴ The correct answer is All whole numbers are integers.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Set of **Whole Numbers** (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

Set of **Integers** (Z) = {..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46be91985385e49744665739cafb2cf441d77ef832c3676d7a541b1b003460a6.png] 

⇒ **Integers** are a collection of **negative numbers**, **zero**, and **positive numbers**.

⇒ **Whole numbers** are a collection of **zero** and **positive numbers**.

⇒ Mathematically, **Z** = {Negative Integers} ∪ **W**.

⇒ This confirms that **W** is entirely contained within **Z**.

⇒ However, **Z** is not a subset of **W** because **negative integers** are not **whole numbers**.

**∴ The correct answer is All whole numbers are integers.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

Counting numbers starting from 1 {1, 2, 3, ...}. All natural numbers are whole numbers and integers.

Rational Numbers (Q)

Numbers that can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. All integers are rational numbers.

Real Numbers (R)

The set of all rational and irrational numbers. The hierarchy is N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R.</p

questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to 0.245?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the number of decimal places: 0.245 has **3 places**.

Place the number over 10³: 245/1000.

Simplify by dividing both by their common factor 5.

245 ÷ 5 = 49 and 1000 ÷ 5 = 200.

**∴ The correct answer is 49/200.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Decimal value = 0.245

**Formula:** Fraction = Number / 10ⁿ (where n = number of decimal places)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecaa187f594aec24a974b0d55051d465ae60debc742e2c5b86eecab20c1d4a5a.png] 

⇒ 0.245 = 245 / 1000

⇒ To simplify, find the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of 245 and 1000.

⇒ 245 = 5 × 49

⇒ 1000 = 5 × 200

⇒ Dividing both numerator and denominator by 5:

⇒ (245 ÷ 5) / (1000 ÷ 5) = 49 / 200

**∴ The correct answer is 49/200.**

**__Additional Information__**

Terminating Decimals

A decimal that ends after a finite number of digits. These can always be expressed as a fraction where the denominator is a power of 10 (10, 100, 1000, etc.).

Simplest Form

A fraction is in its simplest form when the numerator and denominator are **co-prime**, meaning their only common factor is 1.

Decimal to Fraction Rule

Count the decimal places (n) and write the number as the numerator and 10ⁿ as the denominator.</p

questions.question: A baker has 121over2 kg of flour. She uses 3.75 kg for cakes and 42over3 kg for bread. How much flour is left?

Convert all mixed fractions and decimals to a single decimal format.

Total flour = 12.5 kg

Flour used = 3.75 (Cakes) + 4.67 (Bread) ≈ 8.42 kg

Remaining flour = 12.5 − 8.42 = 4.08 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 4.08 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total quantity of flour = 12(1/2) kg

Flour used for cakes = 3.75 kg

Flour used for bread = 4(2/3) kg

**Formula:**

Remaining Flour = Total Quantity − (Flour for Cakes + Flour for Bread)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78240441e13fe474b4c8e37b69e7fdee8f0f1c018f3f53977a44acb530b234fc.png] 

⇒ Total flour = 25/2 = 12.5 kg

⇒ Remaining flour = 12.5 − 8.4167 = 4.0833 kg

Mixed Fraction to Decimal

To convert a mixed fraction like a(b/c), first convert it to an improper fraction (a × c + b) / c, then divide the numerator by the denominator.

Rounding Rules

When subtracting decimals, align the decimal points. If the result has many decimal places, round to the nearest value provided in the options.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is a perfect square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **perfect square** never ends with the digits **2, 3, 7, or 8** at its **unit place**.

Checking the options based on the unit digit:

1057 ends in **7** → Not a perfect square.

23453 ends in **3** → Not a perfect square.

7928 ends in **8** → Not a perfect square.

2500 ends in **0** and has an **even number of zeros** (50 × 50 = 2500).

**∴ The correct answer is 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 1057, (2) 23453, (3) 7928, (4) 2500.

**Property:** A number is a **perfect square** if its square root is an **integer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40f57d4006208bd70a7cfcc9320e94f753622132910b079c01f5a5ea9eadf10c.png] 

Testing each number:

⇒ 1057: Unit digit 7 is not possible for a perfect square.

⇒ 23453: Unit digit 3 is not possible for a perfect square.

⇒ 7928: Unit digit 8 is not possible for a perfect square.

⇒ 2500: Can be written as 25 × 100.

⇒ √2500 = √(25 × 100) = √(5² × 10²)

⇒ √2500 = 5 × 10 = 50.

Since 50 is an integer, 2500 is a **perfect square**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Digit of Perfect Squares

A perfect square always ends with 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. If a number ends in 2, 3, 7, or 8, it is definitely not a perfect square.

Digital Root Property

The **digital root** (sum of digits until a single digit is obtained) of any perfect square is always **1, 4, 7, or 9**.

Trailing Zeros Rule

A perfect square must have an **even number of zeros** at the end. For example, 100, 400, and 2500 are squares, but 10, 1000, and 25000 are not.</p

questions.question: What is the mean proportional between 4 and 16?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean Proportional between two numbers a and b = √(a × b)

Given: a = 4 and b = 16

questions.question: A hemisphere is placed on top of a cylinder with the same base radius. If their combined height is 18 cm and radius is 6 cm, find the total surface area.

Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA of Hemisphere + CSA of Cylinder + Base Area.

TSA = 2πr² + 2πrh + πr² = πr(3r + 2h).

TSA = 3.14 × 6 × (3 × 6 + 2 × 12) = 18.84 × (18 + 24) = 18.84 × 42 = 791.28 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 791.28 cm².**

⇒ Total Surface Area = π × (2 × 6 × 12 + 2 × 6² + 6²)

⇒ Total Surface Area = π × (144 + 72 + 36)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 252 × 3.14

questions.question: In a zoo, there are horse and pigeons. If heads are counted, there are 340 heads and if legs are counted there are 1060 legs. How many pigeons are there?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of pigeons (2-legged) = (4 × Total Heads − Total Legs) ÷ 2

Given: Heads = 340, Legs = 1060

Pigeons = (4 × 340 − 1060) ÷ 2

Pigeons = (1360 − 1060) ÷ 2 = 300 ÷ 2 = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150 pigeons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total heads = 340, Total legs = 1060

Formula Used: Alligation Method or Linear Equations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/382a2964a9b18644efa8cbbc6dbaa0ce3805ea871486ed2a65cd24906b0ccf10.png] 

⇒ Let the number of pigeons be P and horses be H.

⇒ P + H = 340 (Equation 1)

⇒ 2P + 4H = 1060 (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 2: 2P + 2H = 680

⇒ Subtract this from Equation 2: (2P + 4H) − (2P + 2H) = 1060 − 680

⇒ 2H = 380 ⇒ H = 190

⇒ P = 340 − 190 = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150 pigeons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Head and Leg Rule for 4-legged animals

Number of 4-legged animals = (Legs ÷ 2) − Heads. This is a direct variation of the linear equation method.

Alligation Method

Ratio of two groups = (Value₂ − Mean) : (Mean − Value₁), where Mean is the average value per unit.

Logic for 2-legged animals

If all N animals were 4-legged, total legs would be 4N. The difference (4N − Actual Legs) ÷ 2 gives the number of 2-legged animals.</p

• The verb "**insist**" is typically followed by the preposition "**on**" and a **gerund** (verb+ing) or a "that" clause. It is grammatically incorrect to use a "to-infinitive" directly after it.
 
• To correct the sentence, "**to pay**" should be replaced with "**on paying**."

**Correct Sentence:** *"She **insisted on paying** for her meal despite our objections to the contrary."*

• **Common Prepositional Errors:** Many verbs in English require specific prepositions (e.g., "agree with," "depend on," "insist on"). Using an infinitive where a preposition + gerund is required is a frequent grammatical mistake.
